title: Reedholt — the reed-cutters' hamlet in the east marsh
caption: The marsh hamlet four leagues east of Sill, drawn at walking scale: reed-cutters' huts on posts on the dry hummock, the mud-wife's hut with its grey-wool knot, the peat-dry with its drying sods and lifted tally board, peat stacks, the boardwalk over a cut with one plank gone, the peat-hut, the Reed Cut and its cut bundles, and a landing and punt on the Ilm. The river road runs above the marsh toward Sill and Greybank; the marsh road comes down from Mud End, passes the hamlet and goes off toward the Quiet Acre and the Standing Post, both drawn faint or set down in notes. The black peat and the bog-cow are written in the surveyor's margin and drawn nowhere, for a figure would make a thing stand that does not stand. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Frost, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on going into the marsh in pairs, the reed-wolf's five clicks and the man with two fingers gone, borrowed ground and standing reeves, peat and grey weighed under an apron and sealed under a Court name, and the child cutting a first bundle in the dark. An engraved reed-wolf and an engraved count-stick sit in the margin.
